#!/usr/bin/env python3 """ A helper for safely rendering user‑submitted blog posts into a pre‑defined HTML template. """ import html from typing import Final # A minimal but realistic blog format. The placeholders {title} and {body} # will be replaced by the sanitized headline and content. BLOG_FORMAT: Final[str] = """ {title}

{title}

{body}
""" def format_blog_entry(headline: str, content: str) -> str: """ Sanitize and embed a user‑supplied headline and content into the BLOG_FORMAT template. Parameters ---------- headline : str The title of the blog post. It will be HTML‑escaped to prevent injection. content : str The full body of the post. It will be HTML‑escaped and then wrapped in a

tag for each paragraph. Empty lines are treated as paragraph breaks. Returns ------- str A complete HTML document ready to be served. The string is fully escaped, preventing XSS and other injection attacks. Raises ------ TypeError If either argument is not a string. """ if not isinstance(headline, str): raise TypeError(f"headline must be a string, got {type(headline).__name__}") if not isinstance(content, str): raise TypeError(f"content must be a string, got {type(content).__name__}") # Escape headline and content to neutralise any HTML or script injection. safe_headline = html.escape(headline, quote=True) # Split content into paragraphs on double newlines. Each paragraph is escaped # and wrapped in a

tag. This keeps the visual structure of the original # text while ensuring safety. paragraphs = [ f"

{html.escape(paragraph.strip(), quote=True)}

" for paragraph in content.splitlines() if paragraph.strip() # ignore empty lines ] safe_body = "\n".join(paragraphs) # Render the final HTML using the template. rendered = BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=safe_headline, body=safe_body) # Basic sanity check: ensure placeholders have been replaced. if "{title}" in rendered or "{body}" in rendered: raise RuntimeError("Template placeholders were not fully replaced.") return rendered
